hypothesis.text: Replace `_or_opt`'s per-trial destination-list construction and `_route_distance` evaluation with an exact constant-time directed delta. For each source segment, compute its removal gain once from its predecessor/successor boundary arcs and its forward internal cost; for each capacity-feasible destination position, compute insertion cost from destination boundary arcs and the segment's forward or reverse internal cost. Preserve the current source/destination/position/orientation enumeration order, best-gain selection, strict `_EPS` test, reserve polling, and route reconstruction/recalculation/index rebuild only after committing the selected move. The formula must retain directed arc terms so it is correct if distances are asymmetric. This produces the same fully evaluated feasible route-state choice while reducing work in three high-frequency VNS neighborhoods, leaving more deadline budget for ALNS/VNS search. Capacity, unique coverage, implicit-depot routes, and route-count semantics are unchanged, so assess fleet_violation first and then paired final total_distance among equal-fleet feasible outputs.
hypothesis.target_weakness: Embedded VNS consumes about 80% of the fixed solver budget, while `_or_opt` evaluates every length-1/2/3 relocation by allocating a complete destination trial route and recomputing its full route distance. This repeated linear scoring constrains ALNS throughput; a prior isolated evaluation of this same bottleneck reported no fleet regression, two distance-winning pairs and 2, while increasing ALNS iterations from 10,005 to 11,098 on the observed population.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Reduce embedded-VNS scoring overhead and increase completed ALNS iterations without changing feasibility semantics; seek lower final total_distance among equal-fleet outputs.

hypothesis.text: Replace `_or_opt` trial-route scoring with an exact O(1), directed delta calculation. For each source segment, compute its removal gain once from the two removed boundary arcs, replacement boundary arc, and the segment’s directed internal cost; for each capacity-feasible destination position and orientation, compute insertion cost from that position’s boundary arcs and the segment’s forward or reversed endpoints/internal cost. Preserve the current source/position/destination/orientation enumeration order, best-gain choice, strict `_EPS` rule, reserve polling, and route reconstruction/recalculation/index rebuilding only after committing the chosen move. The move selected after a fully completed scan is therefore unchanged even for asymmetric distances, but substantially less per-trial work permits more local-search scans and ALNS trajectories before the same deadline. This is supported by the prior isolated evaluation of this exact bottleneck: no fleet regression, no distance losses on the reached screening pairs, two winning pairs, and 1,093 additional ALNS iterations (11,098 versus 10,005). Capacity, exact customer coverage, implicit-depot routes, route-limit handling, and the public solve contract remain unchanged; evaluate fleet_violation first, then final paired total_distance among equal-fleet feasible outputs.
hypothesis.target_weakness: Embedded VNS dominates the fixed solver budget (about 80% in the available traces), and `_or_opt` repeatedly allocates a full destination trial sequence and recomputes its complete route distance for every insertion position and orientation. This linear repeated scoring occurs in all length-1/2/3 relocation neighborhoods and limits ALNS/VNS throughput.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Reduce embedded-VNS scoring cost and increase completed ALNS iterations while preserving route-state semantics; seek lower final total_distance among feasible outputs with unchanged fleet_violation.
